summary: Moves badge-table rendering into a shared github_render.py utility so the sticky comment's This-run section and the per-review body cannot drift from each other.

pr_summary.headline: Moves badge-table rendering into a shared github_render.py utility so the sticky comment's This-run section and the per-review body cannot drift from each other.

walkthrough.text: format_badge_table, format_badge_tables, and run_stats_primary_cells are extracted into github_render.py with _escape_cell handling pipe, backslash, and line-break sanitization so a stray character in any cell cannot shear a GFM table row.

github_review_body.py deletes the now-redundant private _badge_table and delegates both primary and secondary rows to the shared renderer via format_badge_tables, narrowing the diff to a trivial call-site swap.
github_sticky.py replaces the prose-format _this_run_section with two badge tables, emitting **This run** as a heading followed by the shared primary row and a sticky-specific secondary row.

test_github_badge_tables.py adds 234 lines covering the helper contract (escaping, blank-line separation, empty-row skipping), the ordering rule, the ~ prefix for estimated values, a full snapshot of the sticky's This-run block, and an equality assertion that both surfaces produce the same primary value row.
test_github_sticky_mission_control.py updates the one pinned assertion from the old prose-line format to the new table headers and value rows.

verdict_reasoning.deciding_factor: Nothing blocks the merge. All 41 checklist items answered no. The shared renderer and its escaping logic are correct for all practical inputs, the old _badge_table is fully replaced with no orphaned call sites, and the test suite covers escaping, ordering, blank-line separation, empty-row skipping, and the estimated-vs-reported tilde rule end-to-end through both public build_* surfaces.

file_assessments.overview: Adds _escape_cell, format_badge_table, format_badge_tables, and run_stats_primary_cells as the shared badge-table rendering layer exported from the module.
Deletes the private _badge_table function and its hand-rolled cell assembly, replacing both call sites with the shared format_badge_tables and run_stats_primary_cells imports.
Rewrites _this_run_section from a joined prose string to two badge tables produced by the shared renderer, matching the per-review body's visual layout.
New test file covering the helper contract, the ~ estimation prefix, pipe and backslash escaping, empty-row handling, and an equality assertion that both rendering surfaces agree on the primary row.
Updates the one test that pinned the old prose-line format to assert the new table header and value rows instead.

findings.title: Backslash doubling inside code-chipped model cell
findings.description: _escape_cell doubles all backslashes in its input before escaping pipes. The model cell is passed as the already-backtick-wrapped string '`{model_name}`', so any backslash in the model name gets doubled. Inside a GFM code span, content is rendered literally — '\\' in the source appears as '\\' (two visible characters) to the reader, not '\'. This is a cosmetic regression from the old unescaped _badge_table for the unlikely case where an API returns a model name containing a backslash (e.g. a Windows-path-style identifier or a future provider's naming convention). sanitize_comment_text does not strip or escape backslashes.
findings.cause: The escape order (backslash → pipe → line-break) is correct for preventing a backslash from shielding a pipe, but it also doubles backslashes that are inside code spans where GFM does not process escape sequences — so the doubling is visible.
findings.fix: Confirm whether any supported provider can return a model name containing a backslash. If yes, apply _escape_cell only to the raw text before the backtick-chip wrapping, or strip backslashes from the model name inside sanitize_comment_text. If no provider ever does this, document that assumption in the _escape_cell docstring.
